top_signals.title: Iran War Hikes EU’s Oil Import Bill By $11 Billion Per Month
top_signals.summary: The European Union has been paying $11 billion more to import oil since the Middle East crisis choked crude oil supplies and triggered a global fuel crisis, an analysis by Euronews Business showed on Thursday. The value of the EU’s petroleum imports jumped by 55.8% in the second quarter of 2026, despite the relatively stable volume of imports, according to Eurostat data. Between April and July, right after the closed Strait of Hormuz hiked oil prices, the EU spent an average of $30.7 billion (27.6 billion euros) per month on petroleum oil…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: ECB Holds Rates as Lagarde Announces Early Resignation
top_signals.summary: The European Central Bank kept interest rates on hold at 2.5% as news that President Christine Lagarde will step down from her role early added to concern over energy costs and France's fiscal situation. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports from Frankfurt. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Cyberattack disrupts Belgian tax services before filing deadline
top_signals.summary: The Federal Public Service Finance (FPS Finance), which oversees taxation and other financial administration, said Wednesday that it was investigating the extent of the attack and had temporarily suspended access to MyMinfin, the country's main online platform for managing tax and financial affairs.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: University of New Mexico restores hospital systems, urges no contact with hackers
top_signals.summary: The University of New Mexico was able to restore systems used by its healthcare facilities after a cyberattack forced it to divert ambulances and cancel classes at its medical school.
